summary:
This is a stale re-validation at a3d3860, the merge of uat (SL-040) into SL-042. SL-042's logic is byte-identical to what I validated at b5c2b62. `git diff b5c2b62 a3d3860` over ScanStore.Rollup.cs, Scanning/ and TopLevelTracker.cs is empty. The merge changed only three things: ScanStore.cs remarks, Size/OnDisk becoming internal, and the LargestFilesScaleTests duplicate, which is now built through a repeated ID. So I re-checked the merged tree and the new SL-040 × SL-042 interaction against real data.

**Build and tests**
- Clean Release rebuild (--no-incremental): 0 warnings, 0 errors. The DLLs are fresh.
- Full Core.Tests: 199 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.
- Timing test: 10 reads of 100,000 children took 8.45–11.75 ms, against a 250 ms limit.
- 5M budget test: 652.1 MiB retained, 678.4 MiB peak, against 800 MiB.
- LargestFilesScaleTests: Top(100) over 4.4M entries in 24.6 ms.
- Fitness: all 32 rules hold.

**Real data, throwaway probe**
I ran a throwaway probe in %TEMP% on the merged Core DLL (hash-matched). Its oracles are independent of the store: its own first-seen dedup over the listed IDs, its own charge rule over the raw sizes read by reflection, and its own ranking.
- **C:\Windows** (346,274 entries): dedup flag disagreements 0 of 188,526 files (54,992 later names). Rollup mismatches 0 across 157,748 folders, and root == Totals. ChildrenLargestFirst was correct on every folder; the slowest read was 13.29 ms (WinSxS\Manifests, 38,958 children). LargestFiles.Top(100) matched the probe's own ranking exactly, with no duplicate or repeated ID. Without dedup, 11 later hardlink names would have been in that top 100, so the merged interaction is exercised on real data.
- **C:\Program Files** (87,862 entries, 30 links): the same checks gave 0 mismatches; 5 later names were kept out of the top 100.

**Published app**
- The published single-file exe on C:\Program Files exited 0 with status Completed. Its totals equal the probe's to the byte, the top-level rows sum to the totals, and the largest file on disk is the probe's #1 (1,002,295,296 B).
- The project's window cases passed all 26 non-network cases, including C-003 (hardlinked pair counted once through the window) and SL-040's B-001 to B-008.

**Still open**
- O-025 (owed to build-slice) is not discharged: docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:17-18 still states the pre-SL-042 ChargedSize contract.
- The real-NTFS half of case 8 stays unreachable here: 0 of 168,189 real folders stated a non-zero size of their own.

Worktree left as found; temp files removed.

criteria.how: AChainTenThousandFoldersDeepRollsEveryFileUpToEveryAncestor passed in my Release run on the merged tree.

criteria.criterion: 2. C1: one folder with 100,000 direct children, 1,000 subfolders holding files
3. C1: empty, nested empty, empty root, seeded mixed tree, oracle after every append
criteria.how: All rows of EmptyAndMixedTreesMatchTheOracleAtEveryCut passed. On real data the brute-force oracle matched all 168,189 folders.

criteria.how: OneIdUnderThreeNamesInThreeFoldersIsChargedOnceToTheFirstNamesFolder passed. On real data the store's flag agreed with an independent first-seen dedup on 188,526 + 77,391 files.

criteria.how: ALinkAndAnUnreadableFolderAreLeavesThatAddNothing passed, and the real-tree LinkTests and UnreadableFolderTests passed. On real Program Files (30 links, 2 unreadable) the rollups matched the oracle.

criteria.how: AFolderThatStatesItsOwnSizeAddsNothingOfIt passed. On real data 0 charge-rule disagreements: every folder charges 0.

criteria.how: EachChildsShareIsItsOnDiskBytesOverTheFolders passed. On real data every share equalled OnDisk/parent exactly, and shares summed to 1 within 1e-9.

criteria.criterion: 14. C1: 5,000,000 entries with three rollup columns and a 100,000-child folder
criteria.how: Budget test: 652.1 MiB retained, 678.4 MiB peak, against 800 MiB (GC heap, not private bytes).

planned.evidence: The synthetic brute-force tests (10,000-deep chain, 100,000-wide folder, empty and mixed trees) passed on the merged tree. On real data, an independent oracle over raw leaf sizes matched RolledSize, RolledOnDisk and FilesBelow in all 157,748 C:\Windows and 10,441 Program Files folders (0 mismatches).

The three-names test passed. The store's first-seen flag matched the probe's own first-seen dedup on 188,526/188,526 and 77,391/77,391 real files. SL-040's largest-files list over it contained no later name and no repeated ID, and dedup kept 11 and 5 later names out of the top 100.
The hardlink tests assert FilesBelow at every level, and they passed. The real FilesBelow matched the oracle, which counts every name, in every folder (54,992 later names in C:\Windows).

ALinkAndAnUnreadableFolderAreLeavesThatAddNothing and the real-tree LinkTests and UnreadableFolderTests passed. Real Program Files (30 links, 2 unreadable folders) matched the oracle with every non-file charging 0.
The ordering, stable ties, hand-computed shares and 0-byte-parent tests passed. ChildrenLargestFirst was correct on all 168,189 real folders, with no NaN.
Release timed test: 10 reads of 100,000 children in 8.45–11.75 ms (limit 250 ms). The widest real folder (38,958 children) read in 13.29 ms at most.

obligations.evidence: Owed to build-slice, not discharged. At a3d3860 and in the working tree, docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md:17-18 still says ChargedSize/ChargedOnDisk return Size/OnDisk 'for every other entry'. The merged code charges every Folder 0 (ScanStore.cs:84-99; my real probe found 0 charge-rule disagreements with 'folders charge 0'). It is a doc-only fix, and it does not change any behaviour I measured.
Merged tree, Release: 8.45–11.75 ms over 10 reads, the cold first included.
All real-tree tests passed with rollup assertions. The published exe's top-level rows sum to totals equal to my independent probe's root.
Merged tree: 652.1 MiB retained, 678.4 MiB peak, against 800 MiB.

The m8 semantic merge touchpoint is now exercised. The merged LargestFilesScaleTests builds its duplicate through a repeated ID and passed. On real data Top(100) over the merged store matched an independent dedup-aware ranking exactly.

not_reached: The real-NTFS half of case 8 (a folder that owns a directory allocation) was not checked. 0 of 168,189 real folders on this machine state a non-zero own size. A volume that reports folder sizes (for example the opt-in SMB-LOOPBACK rig or N-001..N-004) was not run.
Process private-bytes peak at 5M entries was not measured against the spike's 1 GiB. The budget test measures GC-heap retained and peak (652.1 / 678.4 MiB) against 800 MiB.
No full-drive scan (about 2.4M files) was run, and no real folder had 100,000 children. My real scans were C:\Windows (346,274 entries) and C:\Program Files (87,862 entries).
Non-NTFS or ID-less volumes (FAT, SMB returning 0 IDs) were not scanned. Only the synthetic tests cover the no-ID sentinels.
Nothing in the window reads ChildrenLargestFirst yet, so the screen's half of the 0.5 s tree budget is unmeasured.

A parallel Scanner, or reads of the rollups from another thread during a scan, is outside the stated contract and was not tested. The no-go spike says first-seen charging would not be repeatable with 16 workers.
eng/rules-harness/harness.py was not run, because it needs the engine's interpreter. plants.json F17 still cites the deleted Scanner.cs:267 line, which is a comment only.
